item.title: Oiclus nanus
item.description:
Oiclus nanus

Oiclus nanus is a small, discreet scorpion living in the humid tropical forests of Grande Terre in Guadeloupe.

It is recognizable by its small size, stocky body, and dark brown to ochre coloration. It mainly inhabits leaf litter, under rocks, and inside decaying logs, where it helps regulate small arthropod populations through active hunting.

This scorpion displays a particular trait common to its entire group: it fluoresces under UV light, turning a bright turquoise blue. This fluorescence, visible only under ultraviolet radiation, is believed to result from chemical components in its cuticle and continues to intrigue researchers. It may help the scorpion detect light, camouflage itself, or communicate, but its exact functions are still under study.
